title: Guides & tools
description: The words in the guides and their interactive tools: the "Your dates" calculator, the fitting bag checklist, the bustle and trouser hem drawings. Leave a field empty to use the original wording. Words in {curly brackets} are filled in automatically, so keep them as they are.

datePast.title: Date has passed
datePast.description: Shown by the "Your dates" calculator and under the wedding date on the contact form.
datePast.default: That date has passed. Check the year?

dateRush.title: Under eight weeks away
dateRush.default: That's under eight weeks. Tell me anyway: I'll say honestly whether I can fit it in, and suggest someone if I can't.

dateBeforeReopen.title: First fitting falls before bridal reopens
dateBeforeReopen.description: {reopens} becomes the reopening time from Site Settings, such as "early 2027".
dateBeforeReopen.default: Your first fitting would fall before bridal reopens ({reopens}). Send a request anyway and I'll tell you honestly whether I can fit it in, with a referral if I can't.

dateAroundReopen.title: First fitting window opens around the reopening
dateAroundReopen.default: Your first fitting window opens right around when bridal reopens ({reopens}), so it's worth joining the waitlist soon.

dateDueNow.title: First fitting is due now (8 to 12 weeks away)
dateDueNow.default: The first fitting is due now, so it's worth booking soon.

dateGood.title: Good timing (bridal open)
dateGood.description: {range} becomes the first fitting dates, such as "Oct 18 to Nov 15, 2026".
dateGood.default: Good timing. Book now and your first fitting lands around {range}.

dateGoodWaitlist.title: Good timing (bridal on the waitlist)
dateGoodWaitlist.default: Good timing. Join the waitlist now and your first fitting lands around {range}.

dateEarly.title: Plenty of time (bridal open)
dateEarly.default: Plenty of time. Book whenever you're ready; fittings start around {range}.

dateEarlyWaitlist.title: Plenty of time (bridal on the waitlist)
dateEarlyWaitlist.default: Plenty of time. Join the waitlist whenever you're ready; fittings start around {range}.

datesLabel.title: Small label at the top
datesLabel.description: The gold label above the calculator's heading, on the timeline guide.

datesHeading.title: Heading
datesHeading.default: Count it back from your wedding

datesIntro.title: Line under the heading
datesIntro.default: Pop in your date and I'll turn the timeline below into real dates you can plan around.

datesPrivacy.title: Note before a date is chosen
datesPrivacy.description: Shown at the bottom of the calculator until a date is picked.
datesPrivacy.default: Nothing is sent anywhere. Your date stays on this device.

datesCountdownDays.title: Countdown: under two weeks
datesCountdownDays.description: {days} becomes the number of days left, such as 9.

datesCountdownWeeks.title: Countdown: two weeks or more
datesCountdownWeeks.description: {weeks} becomes the number of whole weeks left, such as 20.

datesPlanLabel.title: Name of the list of dates (read aloud)
datesPlanLabel.description: Not shown on the page. Screen readers announce it before the list of fitting dates.

datesByDate.title: Date for an open-ended step
datesByDate.description: Used for a step like "12+ weeks". {date} becomes the date, such as "Mar 20, 2027".

datesNow.title: Tag on the step that is happening now

datesPassed.title: Note on a step that has already passed
datesPassed.description: Shown after the dates, following a small dot.

datesPassedSpoken.title: Note on a passed step (read aloud)
datesPassedSpoken.description: Not shown on the page. What screen readers say after a step's dates once it has passed.

datesWedding.title: Last line of the list
datesWedding.description: The wedding day itself, at the end of the list of dates.

datesCtaWaitlist.title: Button: bridal is on the waitlist

datesCtaAsk.title: Button: waitlist, and the date is too soon
datesCtaAsk.description: Used instead of the waitlist button when the date is under eight weeks away or falls before bridal reopens.

bagLabel.title: Checklist heading
bagLabel.description: The gold label at the top of the packing list on the "what to bring" guide. The items themselves are the guide's paragraphs.

bagCount.title: How many are packed
bagCount.description: {count} becomes the number ticked and {total} the number of items.

bagDone.title: Everything is packed
bagDone.default: All packed. See you at the fitting.

bustleStyleLegend.title: Label above the style choices
bustleStyleLegend.description: The style names themselves come from Bustle Styles.

bustleBack.title: Name of the back view
bustleBack.description: Printed in capitals on the drawing, and on the view switch on phones.

bustleSide.title: Name of the side view
bustleSide.description: Printed in capitals on the drawing, and on the view switch on phones.

bustleStageCeremony.title: Stage 1 name
bustleStageCeremony.description: The small gold line above each step's caption on the drawing.

bustleStepCount.title: Step number
bustleStepCount.description: Follows the stage name. {step} becomes the step number and {total} the number of steps (3).

bustleStateDown.title: Train down (read aloud)
bustleStateDown.description: Not shown on the page. What screen readers hear for the drawing and the slider while the train is down.

bustleStateUp.title: Bustled (read aloud)
bustleStateUp.description: Not shown on the page. What screen readers hear once the train is bustled.

bustleDrawingName.title: Name of the drawing (read aloud)
bustleDrawingName.description: Not shown on the page. {style} becomes the style name and {state} one of the two lines above.

bustleSpokenUpdate.title: Announcement on each change (read aloud)
bustleSpokenUpdate.description: Not shown on the page. Screen readers say this whenever the style or position changes.

bustleSliderLabel.title: Name of the slider (read aloud)
bustleSliderLabel.description: Not shown on the page. Screen readers announce it for the slider next to the button.
bustleSliderLabel.default: Train position, from ceremony to reception

bustleAlsoCalled.title: Other names line
bustleAlsoCalled.description: Under the style name, and on the bustle cards. {names} becomes the style's "Also called" from Bustle Styles.

bustleTypicalPoints.title: Label: typical points
bustleTypicalPoints.description: Also used on the bustle cards.

bustlePointsInDrawing.title: How many points the drawing shows
bustlePointsInDrawing.description: Added after the typical points. {count} becomes the number of points drawn.

bustleBestFor.title: Label: best for
bustleBestFor.description: Also used on the bustle cards.

bustleFabric.title: Label: fabric
bustleFabric.description: Also used on the bustle cards.

bustleHowAmerican.title: How it works: American
bustleHowAmerican.description: The paragraph under the style name. The name, other names, points, best for and fabric are edited in Bustle Styles.
bustleHowAmerican.default: The train is lifted and hooked onto the back of the skirt, so it falls in soft poufs over the top.

bustleHowFrench.title: How it works: French
bustleHowFrench.default: The train is tied up underneath the skirt with numbered ribbons, so it tucks under in a cascade.

bustleHowAustrian.title: How it works: Austrian
bustleHowAustrian.default: A cord runs up the center back. Pulling it gathers the train straight up into ruched folds.

bustleHowBallroom.title: How it works: Ballroom
bustleHowBallroom.default: The train folds up underneath all the way round, so the hem sits level with the floor, like a ball gown.

bustleHowDetachable.title: How it works: Detachable train
bustleHowDetachable.default: The train is a separate piece that hooks on at the waist for the ceremony and comes off for the reception.

bustleStepAmerican1.title: American, step 1 (train down)
bustleStepAmerican1.description: The captions on the drawing change as the train lifts: step 1 with the train down, step 2 while it moves, step 3 once it is bustled.
bustleStepAmerican1.default: Loops are sewn under the train.

bustleStepAmerican2.title: American, step 2 (lifting)
bustleStepAmerican2.default: One at a time, from the center, each loop is lifted up the skirt…

bustleStepAmerican3.title: American, step 3 (bustled)
bustleStepAmerican3.default: …and hooked onto a button at the hip.

bustleStepFrench1.title: French, step 1 (train down)
bustleStepFrench1.default: Ribbons are sewn under the train.

bustleStepFrench2.title: French, step 2 (lifting)
bustleStepFrench2.default: From the center out, each ribbon is tucked up underneath the skirt…

bustleStepAustrian1.title: Austrian, step 1 (train down)
bustleStepAustrian1.default: A cord runs through rings up the center back.

bustleStepAustrian2.title: Austrian, step 2 (lifting)
bustleStepAustrian2.default: Pulling the cord gathers the train upward…

bustleStepBallroom1.title: Ballroom, step 1 (train down)
bustleStepBallroom1.default: Ties are sewn all around the underside.

bustleStepBallroom2.title: Ballroom, step 2 (lifting)
bustleStepBallroom2.default: The train folds under, all the way round…

bustleStepBallroom3.title: Ballroom, step 3 (bustled)
bustleStepBallroom3.default: …so the hem sits level, like a ball gown.

bustleStepDetachable1.title: Detachable train, step 1 (train on)
bustleStepDetachable1.default: The train hooks on at the waist.

bustleStepDetachable3.title: Detachable train, step 3 (train off)
bustleStepDetachable3.default: …and the gown underneath is floor length.

hemLegName.title: Leg name
hemLegName.description: How a leg choice is named in the line under the drawing and the notes, such as "Slim leg". {leg} becomes the leg choice.

hemSlantLabel.title: Slanted hem switch
hemSlantLabel.description: The switch below the choices, and the label on its note.

hemSlantShort.title: Slanted hem, in the line under the drawing

hemSlantNote.title: Slanted hem note
hemSlantNote.description: Shown under the choices while the slanted hem is switched on.
hemSlantNote.default: The hem is angled a little longer at the back than the front, so it covers more of the heel without piling up on the shoe. It’s a nice finish on slim trousers.

hemLabelBreak.title: Drawing label: the break
hemLabelBreak.description: Printed in capitals on the drawing, pointing at the fold.

hemLabelNoBreak.title: Drawing label: no break
hemLabelNoBreak.description: Printed on the drawing instead of the one above when "No break" is chosen.

hemLabelHem.title: Drawing label: the hem
hemLabelHem.description: Printed on the drawing, pointing at the back of the hem.

hemDrawingName.title: Name of the drawing (read aloud)
hemDrawingName.description: Not shown on the page. {leg} becomes the leg ("straight"), {shoe} the shoe as said aloud ("a dress shoe") and {break} the break ("a half break" or "no break").
hemDrawingName.default: Side view of a {leg} trouser leg over {shoe}, hemmed with {break}.

hemDrawingNameSlanted.title: Name of the drawing with a slanted hem (read aloud)
hemDrawingNameSlanted.description: Not shown on the page. Used instead of the one above while the slanted hem is on.
hemDrawingNameSlanted.default: Side view of a {leg} trouser leg over {shoe}, hemmed with {break} and a slanted hem.

hemBreakNoneCaption.title: No break: caption
hemBreakNoneCaption.description: Under the drawing while this break is chosen.
hemBreakNoneCaption.default: The hem just skims the top of the shoe, so the leg falls in one clean line with no fold. I love it on slim, modern suits and cropped trousers.

hemBreakNoneSpoken.title: No break: description (read aloud)
hemBreakNoneSpoken.description: Not shown on the page. Screen readers hear it as the drawing's description.
hemBreakNoneSpoken.default: The front of the hem just grazes the top of the shoe with no fold, and the back sits at the top of the heel.

hemBreakQuarterCaption.title: Quarter break: caption
hemBreakQuarterCaption.default: The hem just touches the shoe, leaving a barely-there dimple at the front. It’s the length I suggest most often for suits and chinos today.

hemBreakQuarterSpoken.title: Quarter break: description (read aloud)
hemBreakQuarterSpoken.default: The front of the hem rests lightly on the shoe with a small dimple, and the back covers the top of the heel.

hemBreakHalfCaption.title: Half break: caption
hemBreakHalfCaption.default: One soft fold sits just above the shoe, and the back of the hem covers about half the heel. It’s the classic suit length, and a safe choice if you’re unsure.

hemBreakHalfSpoken.title: Half break: description (read aloud)
hemBreakHalfSpoken.default: One soft horizontal fold sits above the shoe at the front, and the back of the hem covers about half of the heel.

hemBreakFullCaption.title: Full break: caption
hemBreakFullCaption.default: The front folds into a deep crease across the shoe, and the back covers most of the heel. I keep it for fuller, traditional trousers; on a slim leg it just looks too long.

hemBreakFullSpoken.title: Full break: description (read aloud)
hemBreakFullSpoken.default: A deep fold creases across the front above the shoe, and the back of the hem covers most of the heel.

hemShoeDressSpoken.title: Dress shoe: as said aloud
hemShoeDressSpoken.description: Not shown on the page. Fills {shoe} in the drawing's name.

hemShoeDressNote.title: Dress shoe: note
hemShoeDressNote.description: Under the choices while this shoe is chosen.
hemShoeDressNote.default: Dress shoes are low and sleek, so small changes in length show. Most suit hems I pin are pinned over a pair like these.

hemShoeSneakerNote.title: Sneaker: note
hemShoeSneakerNote.default: Sneakers are chunkier and higher at the back, so the same trousers break sooner. I usually take casual pants a touch shorter for them.

hemShoeHeelNote.title: Heel: note
hemShoeHeelNote.default: A heel lifts the back of your foot and tips it forward, so the hem lands somewhere quite different than it does in flats. Bring the shoes you’ll wear, and I’ll pin to those.

hemLegSlimNote.title: Slim leg: note
hemLegSlimNote.description: Under the choices while this leg is chosen.
hemLegSlimNote.default: A slim opening sits right on the shoe, so every bit of break shows. Slim trousers look sharpest with a little break or none.

hemLegStraightNote.title: Straight leg: note
hemLegStraightNote.default: A straight leg is the middle ground. Most suits and chinos are cut this way, and any of these breaks can work.

hemLegWideNote.title: Wide leg: note
hemLegWideNote.default: A wide leg falls past the shoe instead of resting on it, so it barely folds. I usually hem wide legs longer, just clear of the floor.

guidesLabel.title: Guides page: small label
guidesLabel.description: The gold label above the heading on the Guides page.

guidesIntro.title: Guides page: line under the heading
guidesIntro.default: Plain answers to the questions I get asked most, from timelines and bustles to trouser hems.

guidesSeoTitle.title: Guides page: title in search results
guidesSeoTitle.description: Shown on the browser tab and as the headline in Google.
guidesSeoTitle.default: Wedding Dress Alteration Guides | Grace Mae | Pittsburgh

guidesSeoDescription.title: Guides page: description in search results
guidesSeoDescription.description: The short summary under the headline in Google.
guidesSeoDescription.default: Timelines, bustle types, trouser hem lengths and what to bring to a fitting, written by a Pittsburgh bridal seamstress.

guideBackLink.title: Each guide: link back to all guides
guideBackLink.description: The small gold link above every guide's title.

guideQuestions.title: Each guide: closing question
guideQuestions.description: At the bottom of every guide written in the Studio, before the link below.

hemGuideClosing.title: Trouser hem guide: closing line
hemGuideClosing.description: Above the button at the bottom of the trouser hem guide. The rest of that guide is edited in Guides.
hemGuideClosing.default: Not sure which you like? Bring the trousers and the shoes, and we can try a couple of lengths with pins before anything is cut.

hemGuideButton.title: Trouser hem guide: button
hemGuideButton.description: Goes to the contact form with tailoring picked.
